chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say: 'When a man says to another man,
the profit becomes prohibited for him.

key_terms.أَحْسِنْ بَيْعَكَ: Improve your sale / Make your sale better

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a seller's profit if he tells the buyer to 'improve your sale'?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking specific commercial etiquette to the prohibition of profit (*haram al-rabih*). This highlights the Shia juristic view that verbal cues of generosity or concession by the seller can invalidate the legitimacy of the gain, emphasizing that trade is not merely a transaction of goods but a moral contract governed by divine law. It serves as a practical guideline for merchants to ensure their earnings remain pure (*halal*) by maintaining integrity in their verbal interactions during sales.
